card.text: Saturn's second-largest moon, more heavily cratered than Dione and Tethys.

introduction.text: Cassini found a thin exosphere of oxygen and carbon dioxide around Rhea. A 2008 study inferred an orbiting debris disk; a 2010 Cassini imaging search found no rings.

sources.label: Jones et al. 2008
sources.quote: this material is in the form of grains and boulders up to several decimetres in size and orbits Rhea as an equatorial debris disk

sources.label: Tiscareno et al. 2010
sources.quote: Our results contradict an earlier and surprising inference that Rhea, the second-largest moon of Saturn, possesses a system of narrow rings embedded in a broad circum-satellite disk or cloud.

normal.title: Global image mosaic
normal.summary: Detail and shadows vary across the mosaic, which follows a simplified spacecraft shape.

enhanced.title: Enhanced-color composite
enhanced.summary: Colors beyond human vision show real differences between hemispheres; shading and seams remain.

elevation.title: SPC terrain model
elevation.summary: Height above or below a 763.5 km sphere from Cassini's 2025 model, with about 2.15 km spacing.

relative-albedo.title: SPC relative brightness model
relative-albedo.summary: Brightness solved with the Cassini shape, relative to an average of 1; not visible color or reflectance.

shape.title: SPC shape model
shape.summary: Plain surface over a 2,000-face version of Cassini's Q128 shape; small terrain is left out.

infrared.title: Cassini VIMS infrared mosaic
infrared.summary: Photometrically corrected infrared spectra, shown in false color.

ice-absorption.title: Continuum-relative water-ice absorption
ice-absorption.summary: Strength of water-ice absorption, measured from the original spectra.
